reason: The cited evidence shows that active-learning MLPs achieve near-DFT accuracy for energies and forces in refractory high-entropy alloys (E1, E2), but neither passage addresses free-energy evaluation, fusion properties, vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, or electron-vibration coupling. The key premises about capturing these specific entropy terms and the claimed cost reduction are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: MLPs trained on ab initio data can reach near-DFT accuracy for multicomponent alloys
Active learning can generate training sets that cover the relevant configurational space with minimal DFT calculations
MLPs can be used for thermodynamic integration to evaluate free energies
MLPs can capture vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron-vibration coupling if trained on appropriate data
The approach will reduce computational cost by ~1 order of magnitude vs. explicit AIMD/TOR-TILD
